scope: Proposition 2.9 of the manuscript “Every complex K3 surface is Oka” (preprints/Every-complex-K3-surface-is-Oka-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 042 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c35e20c01dcefe76), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let K be a closed circular disc of radius r, or a closed circular annulus with outer radius r, and let f be holomorphic near K × P, where P is a closed polydisc. Suppose that for every ζ on the outer circle there is a coordinate witness neighborhood Vζ for L containing f({ζ} × P). For every R > r and P0 ⋐ int P, one can approximate f uniformly on K × P0 by a map holomorphic near the enlarged disc, respectively annulus with the same inner radius and outer radius R, times P0.
